newsitem.title: USA: FoxMeyer files suit against McKesson, others.
newsitem.headline: FoxMeyer files suit against McKesson, others.

text.p: FoxMeyer Health Corp said Monday it filed suit in a Texas District Court against McKesson Corp and a number of major pharmaceutical manufacturers, claiming they "conspired to drive its subsidiary, FoxMeyer Drug Co, out of business."
FoxMeyer said in a release that it is seeking compensatory damages in excess of $400 million, as well as punitive damages which could amount to $1 billion or more.

FoxMeyer said the complaint alleges that McKesson "misused confidential financial and competitive information to which it had gained access in conceiving, perpetrating, and promoting a plan to drive FoxMeyer out of its industry."

It said that the suit accuses McKesson of exploiting information by "interfering with FoxMeyer Drug's customer and vendor relationships and disrupting its operations in order to effectuate a purchase of its competitor at a significantly distressed price."

FoxMeyer said other defendants include pharmaceutical manufacturers Pfizer Inc, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co, Glaxo Wellcome Plc, Eli Lilly & Co, American Home Products Corp unit Wyeth Ayerst Laboratories Inc, Hoechst AG's Hoechst Marion Rousell Inc, Schering-Plough Corp, Amgen Inc, SmithKline Beecham Plc, Zeneca Group Plc, Johnson and Johnson's Janssen Pharmaceuticals Inc, and Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc.
All of those companies are suppliers to FoxMeyer Drug Co.
McKesson and the other companies named in the suit were not immediately available for comment.
